Trust the process, your brows are healing. 🫰🏼

Right after the SPMU treatment at EVER, the brows may look more defined. In the first few days, the focus is on keeping the brow area dry and protected, avoiding water, sweat, and staying consistent with balm. ‼️

A few days later, peeling may start. It can feel a little uncomfortable, but it’s completely normal. The most important thing is to leave it untouched. 😉

As the healing continues, the peeling slows down and the color begins to soften into a more natural finish. During this phase, it’s best to avoid heat, facials, and heavy sweating. 🌸

It might not look perfect just yet, but everything is going exactly as it should. Book your appointment and start your brow journey ✨

A gentle belly massage before bed can also be part of that routine. Using Contour Treatment Oil from EVERBODY, it helps keep the skin hydrated, supports elasticity, and the calming scent adds a more soothing end to your day. 💖

A little care at night can change how your body feels the next day. ✨

Your baby’s well-being starts with yours. 👶🏻

A fuller-looking hairline doesn't always mean surgery 🤔

When people first hear about Scalp Micropigmentation, many assume it's similar to a hair transplant. But the two work very differently ‼️

Hair transplants involve moving real hair follicles to sparse areas and waiting for the transplanted hair to grow over time.

Scalp Micropigmentation, on the other hand, uses tiny microdots that mimic the appearance of hair follicles ✨without surgery✨ to create the look of fuller hair that blends naturally. 

The best option depends on your goals and hair condition, so understanding the difference is a great first step in finding the right solution for you 😉

When we talk about breast cancer awareness, let's not forget to pay attention to our armpits, too. 🩷 

A lump in your armpit could be a swollen lymph node, a cyst, or something else that needs medical attention. 

Your lymph nodes are part of your immune system, helping your body respond to infections. And while swelling can be a normal immune response, changes around your breast or armpit shouldn't be overlooked. 

That's why knowing your body matters. Pay attention to unfamiliar lumps or changes, and have them checked by a medical professional before considering any lymphatic treatment. 

This Breast Cancer Awareness Month, let's remember that self-care also means staying informed and knowing when to seek help. 🤍
